title: Secure-CHG: A Comprehensive Framework for Robust and Fair Federated Learning via Hybrid Defense and Contribution-Aware Trust

C-a.quote: Data flows to Path A (Serial Statistical Filtering → CHG Contribution Verification) to eliminate high-amplitude outliers and accelerate convergence. ... Early Stage (Path A - Serial Mode): Functions as a secondary defense layer. It performs fine-grained value quantification on nodes that survived Module 1
C-a.locator: Section III-B a) State Monitoring & Routing, and b) Dual-Mode Defense & Evaluation. THREE mechanisms are applied to the same round on Path A, and each carries its own stated defense purpose. (1) The macro cosine-similarity screen: "This framework prioritizes Cosine Similarity over Euclidean Distance [6], [7], [9] as an initial defense to precisely intercept redirection attacks (e.g., sign-flipping) that attempt to divert the global optimization trajectory.", with its own decision rule, "Clients with a negative cosine similarity (sim(j, t) < 0) are excluded. A negative score indicates a directional deviation exceeding 90◦ , reliably signifying a malicious attempt to oppose the majority intent.". (2) The FL-Defender micro screen on last-layer gradient principal components: "Macro screening may miss Targeted Poisoning Attacks (e.g., Backdoors) that embed malicious intent within a tiny fraction of dimensions to evade full-parameter statistical detection [8]. In high-dimensional models (e.g., ResNet-18), these minute alterations are easily masked by the vast majority of benign parameters, rendering full-model cosine similarity ineffective. To address this, FL-Defender specifically analyzes Lastlayer Gradients via Principal Component Analysis (PCA), isolating micro-structural anomalies where attack intent is most concentrated.". These two are DISTINCT under the granularity rule of row 45 -- two independent discriminative signals computed from different inputs, combined in one conjunctive decision, "if sim(k, t) ≥ 0 AND Hkt > Q1t0 t wk = (6) 0, otherwise (identified as malicious)". (3) The CHG-Shapley contribution verification, whose defense purpose is stated in both modes; on Path B it is "Late Stage (Path B - Direct Mode): Functions as the primary line of defense. When gradient norm decay renders traditional statistical features ineffective, this module takes over using the CHG-Shapley mechanism. It identifies and eliminates malicious nodes that are statistically indistinguishable from benign nodes but lack genuine semantic contribution.". EXCISED, and the excision is by the granularity rule rather than by Amendment 3: the EMA reputation stage, "Long-term Reputation Modeling: The system employs an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) to transform instantaneous contributions into a long-term reputation score Tkt , thereby mitigating the impact of intermittent attacks.", and the reputation-modulated aggregation that consumes it, "Regardless of the processing path, the final instantaneous contribution value (Ckt ) is integrated into the unified dynamic trust module.". Its stated purpose IS a defense purpose, so Amendment 3 would admit it; it is not a distinct mechanism, because it temporally smooths the CHG signal rather than contributing an independent signal or an independent decision. AMENDMENT 3 CO-PURPOSE RECORDED for CHG-Shapley: the contributions list gives it a fairness purpose alongside the defense one, "A cascaded statistical filter stabilizes early-stage oscillation, while a trust-modulated aggregation mechanism organically unifies late-stage malicious node defense with benign participant incentivization at the architectural level."

C-b.quote: Macro screening may miss Targeted Poisoning Attacks (e.g., Backdoors) that embed malicious intent within a tiny fraction of dimensions to evade full-parameter statistical detection [8]. In high-dimensional models (e.g., ResNet-18), these minute alterations are easily masked by the vast majority of benign parameters, rendering full-model cosine similarity ineffective. To address this, FL-Defender specifically analyzes Lastlayer Gradients via Principal Component Analysis (PCA), isolating micro-structural anomalies where attack intent is most concentrated.
C-b.locator: Section IV-B; the reason for pairing the second filter with the first is that the first has a named blind spot and the second is chosen to cover it, which is matched threat complementarity with a residual-coverage form. TWO FURTHER ADMISSIBLE REASONS ARE PRESENT IN THE SAME PAPER. Cost complementarity, for the order of the cascade: "To ensure system integrity and balance computational feasibility, we employ a Serial Statistical Filtering approach", coarse macro screening first and the expensive last-layer PCA only on survivors. And a reason of a kind the frame has not seen, indexed by the model's CONVERGENCE STATE rather than by an attack class: the paper names a failure mode of statistical filtering, "we identify a fundamental vulnerability termed “Late-stage Failure.” We demonstrate that as the global model converges, decaying gradient norms render malicious and benign updates morphologically indistinguishable.", and pairs the filter with CHG-Shapley because each covers a different phase, "In contrast, the proposed Secure-CHG framework dynamically orchestrates two orthogonal defenses to circumvent this dual dilemma, achieving a consistently low ASR of 18.84%."

C-c.quote: Average Attack Success Rate (Avg. ASR): The primary indicator of defense robustness (lower is better).

Src-Acc, reported against FedAvg, FedMedian, TrimmedMean, MultiKrum and FLTrust in TABLE II ("P ERFORMANCE C OMPARISON OF D IFFERENT D EFENSE M ECHANISMS (L ATE S TAGE AVG .)"), across three dataset/architecture pairs in "TABLE III G ENERALIZATION P ERFORMANCE ACROSS D IFFERENT DATASETS AND M ODELS", and against backdoor attacks specifically in "TABLE IV ROBUSTNESS AGAINST BACKDOOR ATTACKS (ROUNDS 31-80 AVG .)". The prose reads the composed outcome off those tables, "In contrast, the proposed Secure-CHG framework dynamically orchestrates two orthogonal defenses to circumvent this dual dilemma, achieving a consistently low ASR of 18.84%."

C-d.quote: To explicitly elucidate the individual contribution of each module, we constructed ablation studies featuring two variants: Only CHG (which solely relies on CHG-Shapley for contribution evaluation prior to aggregation) and Only series filters (which exclusively employs FL-Defender for filtering, followed by naive FedAvg aggregation).
C-d.locator: Section VI-C Ablation Studies, with the arms also listed among the baselines as "Ablation Baselines: Pure contribution evaluation (Only CHG) and statistical filtering only (Only series filters)." and their ASR trajectories in "Fig. 8. ASR trends for ablation study comparisons" (arms Only_CHG, Only_series_filters, Secure_CHG). THE CODE RESTS ON THE Only CHG ARM, which removes the UPSTREAM serial filter while the downstream CHG-Shapley, EMA reputation and modulated aggregation are held fixed and the attack is unchanged -- the RKD without-Clustering direction. The paper reads the composed outcome off it and attributes the difference to the removed upstream stage: "First, relying solely on contribution evaluation (Only CHG) exposes a critical weakness during the early stages. As depicted in Fig. 6, without early constraints, malicious clients successfully hijack the initial training phase to accumulate erroneously high contribution scores, culminating in a 67.31% ASR (Fig. 8). Second, standalone cascaded filtering (Only series filters) exhibits severe late-stage ASR instability (33.06% ASR), empirically confirming the “Late-stage Failure” dilemma.". A SECOND, UNDOCUMENTED ROUTE: TABLE II and TABLE III both carry a Krum CHG arm beside the paper's own "Filter CHG (Secure-CHG, ours) Krum CHG", i.e. the same downstream CHG stage fed by Krum instead of the serial filter, which is the FedSAC random-clustering shape of upstream substitution; it is reported with full outcomes and is never defined, motivated or discussed anywhere in the text, so it is admitted under rule 4's benefit of the doubt and the code does not depend on it. THE DECLINED ARM is Only series filters, "To explicitly elucidate the individual contribution of each module, we constructed ablation studies featuring two variants: Only CHG (which solely relies on CHG-Shapley for contribution evaluation prior to aggregation) and Only series filters (which exclusively employs FL-Defender for filtering, followed by naive FedAvg aggregation).", which removes the DOWNSTREAM stage and additionally substitutes the aggregation rule -- two changes at once, in the direction the rubric declines

coder_note:
C-a IS STATE-ROUTED, AND THIS IS THE FIRST ROW IN THE FRAME WHERE THE NUMBER OF MECHANISMS APPLIED TO A ROUND IS A FUNCTION OF A MEASURED STATE OF THE RUN. The paper's own headline framing would code C-a = NO: the abstract says the filter "stabilizes optimization during the early oscillatory phase, while a novel CHG-Shapley mechanism takes over during late-stage convergence", and Section III-B says the late path "The system shifts to Path B (Direct CHG Contribution Verification), bypassing statistical filters to identify covert malicious nodes at the semantic level via CHG-Shapley." -- if that were the whole architecture, the two mechanisms would ALTERNATE by round and would never be applied together to the same round, which is what C-a's frozen text requires. But it is not the whole architecture. Path A, taken in every early-stage round, is "Data flows to Path A (Serial Statistical Filtering → CHG Contribution Verification) to eliminate high-amplitude outliers and accelerate convergence.", and CHG-Shapley there runs on the filter's survivors within the same round: "Early Stage (Path A - Serial Mode): Functions as a secondary defense layer. It performs fine-grained value quantification on nodes that survived Module 1". So early-stage rounds compose three mechanisms and late-stage rounds compose one. I coded C-a = YES on Path A and recorded Path B, rather than the reverse, because C-a asks whether two or more mechanisms are applied together to the same round and Path A is an unambiguous instance of that; the two paths are two facts about the system, not two readings of one sentence, so rule 3 is not engaged. A5 must carry this as a THIRD STRUCTURAL KIND on the parallel-versus-sequential axis: not parallel, not fixed-sequential, but CONDITIONALLY ROUTED. It also bears on our own framing, because Prop. prop:identification_full presupposes a pipeline whose composition does not change during the run.

THE GRANULARITY RULE AND AMENDMENT 3 POINT OPPOSITE WAYS HERE, FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND THE ORDER IN WHICH THEY APPLY DECIDES THE COUNT. The EMA reputation stage has a stated DEFENSE purpose -- "Long-term Reputation Modeling: The system employs an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) to transform instantaneous contributions into a long-term reputation score Tkt , thereby mitigating the impact of intermittent attacks." -- so Amendment 3, read alone, would count it toward C-a's two-or-more. The granularity rule of row 45 excludes it, because it smooths the CHG signal into a weight rather than contributing an independent discriminative signal or an independent decision about an update. I applied DISTINCTNESS FIRST AND PURPOSE SECOND, which is the only order that makes sense of the two rules -- Amendment 3 asks whether a distinct component counts, and it presupposes that the component is distinct -- but the ordering was not written down before this row, and A5 must disclose it as such. The count does not depend on it: C-a = 3 without the EMA stage and would be 4 with it.

CHG-SHAPLEY IS A SECOND DUAL-PURPOSE COMPONENT, AFTER FedSAC's CLUSTERING. Its defense purpose is explicit in both modes ("Late Stage (Path B - Direct Mode): Functions as the primary line of defense. When gradient norm decay renders traditional statistical features ineffective, this module takes over using the CHG-Shapley mechanism. It identifies and eliminates malicious nodes that are statistically indistinguishable from benign nodes but lack genuine semantic contribution."), and the contributions list gives it a fairness purpose in the same breath: "A cascaded statistical filter stabilizes early-stage oscillation, while a trust-modulated aggregation mechanism organically unifies late-stage malicious node defense with benign participant incentivization at the architectural level.". Amendment 3 counts it on the defense quotation and the co-purpose is recorded. Unlike FedSAC, where the paper elsewhere describes the dual-purpose component as "conducted only for noise minimization" when its defense role is stripped, nothing here retracts the defense purpose, so this instance is easier than FedSAC's.

THREE ADMISSIBLE PAIRING REASONS IN ONE PAPER, AND ONE OF THEM IS A NEW SUB-KIND. Cost complementarity governs the ORDER of the cascade (cheap full-vector cosine screen first, expensive last-layer PCA on survivors). Matched threat complementarity with a residual-coverage form governs its CONTENT (the macro screen misses backdoors that hide in a few dimensions, so the micro screen is chosen for exactly those). And the filter-versus-CHG pairing is justified by a reason indexed by the model's CONVERGENCE STATE rather than by an attack class: statistical morphology works while updates are far apart and fails once they are not ("we identify a fundamental vulnerability termed “Late-stage Failure.” We demonstrate that as the global model converges, decaying gradient norms render malicious and benign updates morphologically indistinguishable."), so the two mechanisms cover different PHASES of the same run ("In contrast, the proposed Secure-CHG framework dynamically orchestrates two orthogonal defenses to circumvent this dual dilemma, achieving a consistently low ASR of 18.84%."). Every prior C-b in the frame partitions the ATTACK space; this one partitions the RUN. A5 should report it as REGIME COMPLEMENTARITY, a fourth form of complementary coverage alongside threat, adversarial and residual, and note that it is the only pairing reason in the frame whose partition is temporal.

THE Fig. 6 / Fig. 7 COMPARISON IS THE FRAME'S MOST DIRECT EXTERNAL MEASUREMENT OF A DOWNSTREAM MECHANISM'S OWN SIGNAL CONDITIONED ON THE PRESENCE OF THE UPSTREAM STAGE, AND A3 MUST ENGAGE IT. Fig. 6 plots the CHG contribution values of every client over time for Only CHG; Fig. 7 plots the same quantity for the full pipeline. The paper reads the pair as a mechanism: "A direct comparison between Fig. 6 and Fig. 7 distinctly illuminates the mechanism behind this success. During early training, morphology-based statistical defenses (e.g., the FLDefender filter in Section IV-B) intercept anomalous updates. Crucially, this early-stage intervention effectively prevents attackers from accumulating unwarranted trust; consequently, the late-stage contribution scores of malicious nodes are fundamentally suppressed (Fig. 7).". That is not a composed-accuracy ablation -- it is the downstream stage's INTERNAL discriminative signal, measured with and without the upstream filter, and it finds a large effect. Composition interaction now has an eighth external treatment and a second empirical one that inspects the downstream signal itself; DDFed measured the same shape and found NO effect of upstream DP noise on downstream detection, and this paper measures it and finds the signal transformed. WHAT OUR CONTRIBUTION ADDS OVER IT, stated so A3 can say it plainly rather than leave the omission to be read as agreement with the novelty charge: the upstream stage here is present or absent, not varied across a graded family; the outcome read is a single scalar and a pair of qualitative figures rather than an ORDERING of arms; there are no repetitions, no intervals and one dataset with one attack; and the dependence is used as a design justification rather than made the object of study. EnCAgg (2605.22506) remains the closest analogue overall because it also changes the design in response; this paper is the closest on the measurement itself.

A NUMERIC-MAPPING CAVEAT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT ALMOST PUT WRONG NUMBERS IN THIS RECORD. TABLE II's twenty-seven cells extract COLUMN-MAJOR as one undelimited numeric block, and the block is interposed between two DIFFERENT and differently-ordered copies of the row-label list -- a figure legend reading "FedAvg FedMedian TrimmedMean MultiKrum FLTrust Krum_CHG Secure_CHG" and the table's own "Filter CHG (Secure-CHG, ours) Krum CHG". I reconstructed it (Only CHG 67.31 ASR, Only series filters 33.06, Secure-CHG 18.84, Krum CHG 20.82) and cross-checked every value against a prose sentence or against TABLE III's CIFAR-10 column before believing it; the three arm ASRs quoted in this record all come from prose, and NO CODE DEPENDS ON THE TABLE MAPPING. A5 should name this hazard separately from column splicing and from page-boundary reordering: DUPLICATED LABEL LISTS IN DIFFERENT ORDERS around a column-major numeric block. Worth noting for A4 as a side effect: the upstream SUBSTITUTION arm (Krum CHG, about 2 points of ASR) and the upstream REMOVAL arm (Only CHG, about 48 points) differ by more than an order of magnitude, so a paper can run an upstream contrast and find almost nothing while the same pipeline is enormously sensitive to whether the upstream stage is there at all.
